blocker:
Exact commands attempted and their verbatim (redacted) output: (1) `agent status` -> "Starting login process...
Checking authentication status...
✓ Login successful!
Logged in (unable to fetch user details)
(exit code 0)"; (2) `agent about` -> "User Email: Not logged in" (exit code 0); (3) `agent models` / `agent --list-models` (default, and with `--model grok-4.5`, and with `--model definitely-not-a-real-model`) -> "Loading models…
No models available for this account.
(exit code 0)" in all three cases. Net effect: the CLI self-reports a successful login but cannot resolve a user identity or any usable model for the account. `agent --print` (`--output-format json` and separately `stream-json`, both `--mode ask --trust`) was run twice and both failed free at the auth gate with "Authentication required" before any billed turn could start (see preflight.md's `agent --print` auth-gate check); beyond those two zero-cost calls, `--print` was intentionally not invoked further, to avoid risking a billed turn against an account with no confirmed model access. Concrete preconditions to unblock: (a) a reachable CURSOR_API_KEY (or equivalent bearer credential) must be present in the session env so headless auth does not depend on the interactive `agent login` browser flow, which a sandboxed headless worker cannot complete; (b) the Cursor account tied to that credential must have at least one model provisioned/entitled, since `agent models` currently returns zero models regardless of --model value and there is no local keychain/session-store access available to this sandboxed worker to inspect or repair the account's session state directly.
